transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Alvarez (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Dr. Marcus Li (ElmCare Head of Data), Sonia Patel (ElmCare Dir. ML Ops), Ethan Reed (ElmCare CTO)

Summary (auto): POC for clinical summarization/triage assistant. Define quality eval plan: golden prompts, regression suite, hallucination and format checks, scoring axes, and schedule for benchmarks across hosted + dedicated.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. This is Jordan from Redwood, AE. Priya and I will run through the POC scoping for ElmCare's summarization project. How's everyone doing?
00:08 Marcus: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get this moving.
00:11 Jordan: Great. Quick agenda - 1 confirm success criteria, understand workload shape, agree on benchmark plan and timeline, and then dig into the quality evaluation approach - 1 golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring. Sound ok?
00:22 Sonia: Yep, that's what we want. I'd like to emphasize regulatory constraints - we need audit logs and KMS for keys.
00:29 Priya: Totally. We'll note that for the private deployment path. For the quality plan, we usually start with a 20-30 golden prompt set covering core workflows, edge cases, and PHI redaction checks.
00:41 Ethan: Quick ask - can that include both short triage-style prompts and longer note summarization?
00:46 Priya: Absolutely. We typically bucket prompts: triage (1-3 sentences), encounter summary (100-300 words), and complex multi-visit summarization.
00:55 Jordan: Marcus, what's your initial success criteria? Latency, accuracy, hallucination tolerance?
01:00 Marcus: Good question. Primary is factual accuracy and no hallucinations on medication or diagnoses. Secondary is formatting and structured output for EHR ingestion. Latency target is sub-2s for triage prompts in peak mode, but we're flexible if cost is lower.
01:14 Sonia: And for compliance - we need full audit trails and an ability to pin model versions for audits.
01:19 Priya: We support that. For the POC we can run both hosted and a Dedicated pool to compare throughput and unit cost.
01:26 Jordan: OK, workload sizing - Sonia, estimated QPS or concurrent users?
01:30 Sonia: We'll start small: about 150 triage requests/day and 50 summarizations/day for the pilot, but production could be 2-3k/day. Concurrent during clinic hours maybe 20-30.
01:40 Priya: Good, that's lightweight. For benchmarking we recommend simulating 1x, 5x, and 10x pilot load to understand autoscaling and batching impacts.
01:49 Jordan: Benchmarks - we propose three tracks: quality (accuracy/regression), latency/cost (hosted vs dedicated), and safety (hallucination/PII leakage). Any objections?
01:58 Marcus: No objections. For quality, we need a scoring rubric - what do you recommend?
02:02 Priya: We use a hybrid scoring approach: automated passes for format and required-field presence, token-level overlap metrics (ROUGE/BLEU for structure), and human graded checks for factual correctness and hallucination severity. Each golden prompt gets example "expected" outputs and a severity weighting.
02:18 Jordan: Example: a medication hallucination would be a critical failure - score zero for that prompt; formatting deviations may be partial pass.
02:26 Marcus: Makes sense. How many human evals per prompt?
02:29 Priya: For the POC: 3 human raters per prompt for initial set of ~25 prompts. That gives decent inter-rater signal. We can supplement with automated NLI-based hallucination detectors for scale.
02:40 Sonia: We need to be careful with NLI detectors - they can have false positives on clinical paraphrase.
02:45 Priya: Agreed. We'll treat automated flags as triage for human review rather than ground truth.
02:50 Ethan: What about regression tests? We have an existing set of ground-truth summaries for past notes, about 200 examples. Can we use those?
02:57 Jordan: Yes, please. Please share those - we'll incorporate into the regression suite. For the golden prompts, we'll craft specific edge cases (ambiguous timeline, med list consolidation, negated findings).
03:09 Marcus: Hallucination checks - beyond meds/diagnosis, also avoid inventing procedures or dates.
03:14 Priya: We'll include targeted hallucination tests: prompt templates that intentionally encourage model to guess missing info; we expect zero hallucinated entities in outputs.
03:22 Jordan: Format checks - you mentioned EHR ingestion. Do you need JSON with specific fields?
03:26 Marcus: Yes, we expect a JSON payload: summary_text, meds_list (array with name/dose), problems (list), and suggested_action. Strict schema required.
03:34 Priya: For POC we'll validate schema via automated JSON schema checks and sample-length heuristics. Failures will be counted as format errors in scoring.
03:41 Jordan: Scoring approach - propose weighted rubric: factual correctness 50%, hallucination severity 20%, format/schema correctness 20%, latency/throughput 10%. Any tweaks?
03:52 Sonia: That seems fine but can we make hallucination severity higher, maybe 30%? Med hallucinations are critical for compliance.
03:58 Marcus: I support that - put 30% on hallucination, reduce latency to 5%.
04:03 Priya: Updated proposed weights: factual correctness 50, hallucination 30, format 15, performance 5. We'll surface both per-prompt and aggregate scores.
04:12 Jordan: Timeline - here's a suggested plan:
- 2026-09-24: Redwood sends draft golden prompts and scoring matrix
- 2026-09-25: ElmCare sends redacted sample data and 5 representative live prompts
- 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-01: Benchmark runs (hosted baseline + dedicated config)
- 2026-10-02: Review call with initial scores and action items
04:31 Marcus: That's aggressive but doable. We may need 48 hours to sanitize PHI.
04:36 Jordan: Totally understood. We'll accept redacted samples if full redaction is slower.
04:40 Sonia: Deployment mode - we'll try hosted first to validate quality, then dedicated if latency/cost or data residency requires it.
04:47 Priya: We'll include both in benchmark matrix - same model checkpoint where possible to isolate infra differences. If model variants are needed for quantization, we'll document that as part of the run.
04:58 Ethan: Can we run a short smoke test internally with our team before the official benchmark?
05:01 Jordan: Yes, we'll provision a small sandbox and share credentials. Expect a short read-only key for initial tests.
05:07 Marcus: One more thing - auditability and model pinning: we need a way to tie results to model version and config for compliance.
05:13 Priya: Redwood's outputs include model_version, config hash, and an audit log for each request. We'll surface that in the benchmark reports.
05:20 Jordan: Great. Any blockers or open risks?
05:23 Sonia: Data sharing timeline is the only risk. Also curious about the cost delta between hosted and dedicated for the pilot.
05:29 Jordan: We'll include a rough cost delta in the SOW and actual measured cost in the benchmark report.
05:34 Marcus: Ok. I think we're aligned.
05:36 Jordan: Recap of next steps - Jordan to send draft plan and SOW, Priya to share golden prompt examples and regression scaffolding, ElmCare to share redacted samples and 5 prompts. Schedule benchmark run for 9/28-10/1 and review 10/02.
05:50 Ethan: Thanks all, look forward to the plan.
05:52 Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links to the plan and the sandbox credentials. Bye.

End of transcript.

Notes / artifacts referenced:
- Redwood: POC SOW template (link shared post-call)
- Draft golden prompts doc (to be shared)
- ElmCare redacted samples (to be provided by ElmCare)
- Benchmark spreadsheet (Redwood to run and fill)

Quality eval plan highlights (extracted):
- Golden prompts: ~25 prompts covering triage, encounter summary, multi-visit consolidation, negation and med lists.
- Regression tests: include ElmCare's 200 ground-truth examples + golden prompt set. Automated + human-in-loop grading.
- Hallucination checks: targeted prompts for meds/diagnoses/procedures/dates; automated NLI flags + human verification.
- Format checks: JSON schema validation for required fields (summary_text, meds_list, problems, suggested_action).
- Scoring: weighted rubric (factual 50 / hallucination 30 / format 15 / perf 5) with per-prompt and aggregate dashboards.
- Benchmark matrix: hosted baseline, dedicated pool at pilot and 5x pilot load, autoscaling behavior and cost per 1k tokens evaluated.

Action items (reiterated):
- Jordan: Send draft quality eval plan, SOW, and schedule (due 2026-09-24)
- Priya: Share golden prompt examples and regression scaffolding (due 2026-09-24)
- Dr. Marcus Li: Provide 5 representative prompts and redacted samples (due 2026-09-25)
- Sonia Patel: Confirm infra constraints and preferred deployment path (due 2026-09-25)
